Location: Harvey Lock, Harvey (GIWW west of New Orleans, Harvey Canal / Mississippi River)
Item: UPDATE: Harvey Lock reported paused again Oct 10 – status unclear
Details: The sheet listed Harvey Lock as reopened Oct 5. A barge-industry river report seen on Oct 13 said Harvey Lock operations were paused again at 1:30pm Oct 10 because of reverse-head conditions (low Mississippi River), with no Corps estimate for reopening. Today's (Oct 20) version of that report no longer lists Harvey Lock, which may mean it has reopened – no official reopening notice found. Why it matters: if you're heading east-west through New Orleans on the GIWW, don't count on Harvey; Algiers Lock is the usual detour.
Notes: What to do: Call Harvey Lock before you commit to the route – lockmaster (504) 862-1061, lock wall (504) 366-5187 (numbers from the Aug 2026 Coast Guard notice). Plan on Algiers Lock as the alternative. Uncertainty: the Oct 10 pause comes from American Commercial Barge Line's river report, not a Corps bulletin, and today's report is silent on Harvey.

Location: Leland Bowman Lock, near Intracoastal City (GIWW, Vermilion Parish)
Item: Leland Bowman Lock closed – log jammed in the gate
Details: Unplanned closure since 2am Oct 20: a log is keeping the gates from working properly, and crews are on site trying to remove it. As of 5:30am, 22 tows were waiting with an average delay of about 15 hours. Why it matters: this is the main GIWW lock between Morgan City and the Calcasieu – with a long commercial queue, a recreational boat can expect a long wait even after it reopens.
When: Since 2am Tue Oct 20 2026; no reopening time given
Notes: What to do: Call the lock before you arrive and ask about the queue; consider waiting at Intracoastal City or Delcambre rather than idling at the lock. Check the USACE New Orleans District notices for an all-clear. Source is a barge-industry report; no Corps bulletin found yet. Same stretch as the Schooner Bayou restricted locking already in the sheet.

Location: Berwick Bay BNSF railroad bridge, Morgan City (Atchafalaya River mile 17.5)
Item: Morgan City BNSF rail bridge closures for repairs
Details: American Commercial Barge Line's river report lists the BNSF railroad bridge at Morgan City as closing for repairs 8am Wed Oct 21 through midnight Thu Oct 22, and again 8am Wed Nov 4 through midnight Thu Nov 5. Why it matters: the GIWW crosses Berwick Bay right at Morgan City; sailboats and taller boats that need the bridge raised may not get through during these windows.
When: 8am Oct 21 – midnight Oct 22 2026; 8am Nov 4 – midnight Nov 5 2026
Notes: What to do: If you need the lift span, plan to cross before 8am Wednesday or after Thursday night, and repeat for Nov 4–5. Confirm with the bridge tender on VHF before arriving. Uncertainty: the source lists this as a 'closure for repairs' and doesn't say whether low boats that fit under the closed span may still pass; no Coast Guard notice found yet.

Location: Calcasieu Lock, near Lake Charles (GIWW, Calcasieu Parish)
Item: Calcasieu Lock: weekday daytime closures through about Oct 30
Details: North chamber wall repairs close the lock Monday–Friday 7am–7pm, scheduled through approximately Oct 30 (the earlier end date was Sept 18). Industry expected delays of 3–5 days; on Oct 20 tows were averaging about 12 hours in the queue. Why it matters: if you're crossing west Louisiana on the GIWW, a daytime weekday arrival means waiting until evening – plan to lock through at night or on the weekend.
Notes: What to do: Time your arrival for after 7pm, or Saturday/Sunday. Call the lock ahead to check the queue. End date is approximate – check USACE New Orleans District notices around Oct 30.

Location: Bayou Sorrel swing bridge (LA 75), Port Allen–Morgan City Alternate Route, Iberville Parish
Item: Damaged Bayou Sorrel swing bridge opens for boats only in set windows
Details: After a tow hit the swing bridge, it opens to boat traffic only twice a day – 11pm–5am and 10am–1pm – while it's closed to cars. No end date has been given. Why it matters: if you're taking the Alternate Route between Port Allen and Morgan City and need the bridge to swing, you have to arrive inside those windows or wait.
When: Daily since Oct 2 2026: 11pm–5am and 10am–1pm; no end date
Notes: What to do: Plan to reach the bridge between 10am and 1pm (or overnight 11pm–5am). Barge-line report says it's 'intermittently closed' to marine traffic, and another local report gave different hours (9am–noon), so call the bridge on VHF before arriving. Map point is the Bayou Sorrel community, approximate.

Location: Colorado River Locks, near Matagorda (GIWW mile 441.5)
Item: Colorado River Lock closed daily for gate repairs – through Oct 23
Details: West lock sector-gate repairs close the lock daily 8am–6pm (weekends and holidays excluded) from Aug 19 through Oct 23. On Oct 20 tows averaged about 17 hours waiting. Why it matters: the last few days of a long daytime closure on the main Texas GIWW – plan to pass in the evening or on the weekend.
Notes: What to do: Arrive after 6pm or Saturday/Sunday until Fri Oct 23. Check back after Oct 23 for normal operations.

Location: Brazos River Floodgates, near Freeport (GIWW mile 401)
Item: Brazos River Floodgates repair restrictions extended to Dec 28
Details: Repair restrictions at the floodgates have been extended and stay in place Monday–Friday 7am–7pm through Dec 28, 2026. Why it matters: the Brazos crossing is already a tricky spot for slow boats (current across the GIWW); weekday daytime restrictions add waiting time on a Freeport–Matagorda run.
Notes: What to do: Plan the crossing for evenings or weekends, and call the floodgate tender on VHF before arriving. The source doesn't say exactly what the restriction is (one-way traffic, size limits or closure) – ask the tender. Map point approximate.

Location: Orange Beach Event Center at The Wharf, Orange Beach (GIWW)
Item: AGLCA Fall Rendezvous – Great Loopers gather at The Wharf
Details: America's Great Loop Cruisers' Association holds its Fall Rendezvous at The Wharf in Orange Beach, right on the Loop route. It's officially sold out (waitlist open) and there are no day passes this year. Why it matters: expect a crowd of Loop boats on the Alabama GIWW that week and slips at The Wharf Marina tied up by registrants.
Notes: What to do: Passing through that week? Reserve a slip elsewhere in Orange Beach/Gulf Shores early. Waitlist is on the AGLCA page. Map point approximate (The Wharf).

Location: Palm Coast – Atlantic ICW from the North Cut (Hammock Beach Bridge) to Grand Haven
Details: Boats of any size, decorated or not, parade along the Intracoastal from the North Cut to the gazebo at Grand Haven. Viewing at Waterfront Park and the St. Joe Walkway Trailhead under the Hammock Beach Bridge. Why it matters: a friendly one to join if you're on the Atlantic ICW that weekend – and expect parade traffic in that stretch Saturday evening.
Notes: What to do: Register through the City of Palm Coast online form; all captains must attend a pre-parade meeting. Map point approximate (Hammock Beach Bridge).

Location: Gulfport (Boca Ciega Bay) – starts at Gulfport Municipal Marina
Item: Boca Ciega Yacht Club Holiday Boat Parade
Details: Decorated boats leave Gulfport Municipal Marina and run past Clam Bayou, Osgood Point, Williams Pier, the Gulfport Casino and Pasadena; tied to the Gulfport Police 'Operation Santa' toy drive. Viewing from Gulfport Beach, Veterans Park, the pier and waterfront restaurants.
Notes: What to do: Contact Boca Ciega Yacht Club to enter a boat. Same night as the Panama City Boat Parade of Lights already in the sheet.
